method: Hull speed is estimated as v = 1.34*sqrt(LWL) in knots with LWL in feet, equivalent to about 2.43*sqrt(LWL) in knots with LWL in metres. The speed-length ratio is v(kn)/sqrt(LWL(ft)) and the Froude number is v/sqrt(g*LWL) with g = 9.80665 m/s^2; at the hull-speed estimate the speed-length ratio is 1.34 and the Froude number about 0.40. The planned speed is classified as displacement speed at or below 95 percent of the estimate, at hull speed from 95 to 105 percent, above hull speed from 105 to 160 percent, and the planing regime beyond 160 percent. Waterline length converts from metres or feet, planned speed from knots, km/h or mph, and inputs are limited to 1-100 m and 0-100 kn. The coefficient is an empirical planning guideline for displacement hulls in calm water: displacement, hull shape, slenderness, trim and sea state are not modelled, and multihulls, slender hulls and planing hulls exceed it. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Larsson, L. and Eliasson, R. E., Principles of Yacht Design, 4th edition, Adlard Coles, 2014
Froude, W., 'On the Leading Phenomena of the Wave-Making Resistance of Ships', Transactions of the Institution of Naval Architects, 1881
